notes: Scope: the six ACME investigations BRE (PSI-20), CLD Flame (PSI-21), E-FIELD Flames (PSI-22), Flame Design (PSI-10), s-Flame (PSI-23) and CFI-G (PSI-159). Each psi_id and psi_url was checked against research/psi-investigations.json. All linked flight investigations are microgravity; this review found no partial-gravity experimental result in the cited material.

Independent verification, 2026-11-14: all 75 input findings passed quotecheck --refetch, including the live NTRS abstract for ACME-032. All 75 were then read in context and retained with substantive changes, not merely a verified flag. The 6 investigation records and their field citations were reviewed separately. See acme.rejects.md for every changed element and the validation commands.

Quotes use the exact quotecheck normalisation: Unicode NFKC, folded typographic quotes/dashes, removed soft hyphens and collapsed whitespace. Twenty-two finding quotes were widened or corrected. ACME-001 and ACME-003 now cite the same prose in the live-checked BRE final-report PDF instead of escaped JSON record text.

Conditions are confined to the quoted result. Unquoted gravity, platform, fuel, airflow, oxygen and pressure were set to null rather than inherited from the investigation or another paragraph. Table rows ACME-073 and ACME-074 are complete structured CSV citations, checked with their column headers. Oxygen and pressure from those rows remain in the claims, but their numeric conditions are null because the quote lacks the required units/column labels. Oxygen mole fraction 0.39 remains in ACME-067 and ACME-070 quotes and claims, with o2_percent null under the literal build gate.

BRE material conclusions are gas-burner emulations and material inferences, not direct burns of all the named plastics. ACME-026 reports a transient-model comparison, ACME-032 is SLICE precursor evidence, ACME-052 is DESI drop-tower precursor evidence, and the roughly 100,000 s Flame Design value is an infinite-domain model time, not a flight burn duration. ACME-034 proposes a partial-gravity proxy, and ACME-051 is an operational concentration limit.

Preliminary results and source hedges are preserved, including methane/large-flame exceptions in BRE, incomplete computational confirmation of s-Flame extinction mechanisms, apparent rather than proven flash re-ignition, and the kinetic-extinction qualification after the hydrogen radiative-extinction result.

decision_hint and earth_instinct are VESTA interpretation, not NASA quotations. Hints were narrowed to the cited observations or explicitly labelled analytical limits; source-free operating procedures, detector thresholds, generic cabin guarantees and a denial of observed electric-field blowout were removed. environment_relevance remains an author relevance tag, not proof of a tested habitat atmosphere or gravity.

Live source checks: 11 cached PDFs were byte-identical to downloads from NTRS or PSI; their cached text matched pdftotext -layout after normalisation. The NASA ACME fact-sheet PDF contained its entire cached text body and all cited finding quotes. The live NASA cool-flames page contained every original finding quote although the HTML bytes had changed. Requests were serial, with a one-second pause. Two guessed NTRS PDF filenames initially returned 404; the actual download paths from saved NTRS metadata succeeded. No source was rejected for those guessed-path failures.

Not re-fetched in this pass: PSI metadata JSON records and experimental CSV tables. Their saved NASA files and catalog mappings were checked locally. This is the weakest provenance check remaining; the live report comparisons do not establish live byte identity of those JSON/CSV endpoints.

Validation includes a negative quote control: appending a unique absent sentinel to ACME-001 caused quotecheck to return 1 and FAIL. The final unmutated file must return 0. The actual build sentence and conditions gate functions were executed read-only; no full build, publication or browser audit is claimed.

ACME-034 includes a same-report conditions_quote identifying the ISS experiment. The result quote says zero gravity while proposing partial gravity as a future proxy; the extra literal context lets the build retain microgravity without misclassifying the proposal as a partial-gravity test.

investigations.name: Flame Design
investigations.full_name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Flame Design
investigations.hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) with the ACME chamber insert and a porous stainless-steel spherical burner
investigations.years: 2019-2022 (ISS tests April to July 2019 and October 2021 to February 2022)
investigations.pi: Richard L. Axelbaum (Washington University in St. Louis)
investigations.objectives: Obtain soot-inception limits and extinction limits of quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames as functions of flow rate, stoichiometric mixture fraction, amount of inert and pressure, with detailed measurements, and evaluate whether steady flames can exist.
fuels: ethylene (C2H4), pure and diluted with nitrogen
investigations.sample_geometry: Porous stainless-steel spherical burner in the chamber: normal flames (fuel flows from the burner into an oxygen/nitrogen atmosphere) and inverse flames (oxygen/nitrogen flows from the burner into a nitrogen/ethylene atmosphere).

conditions.o2_percent: normal flames: ambient oxygen mole fraction 0.2 to 0.38 (limit 40%); inverse flames: burner supply oxygen mole fraction 0.4 to 0.85
conditions.pressure: published extinction results at 1 bar; chamber pressure was also varied (the PSI inverse-flame table lists an initial pressure of 3.0 atm in some tests)
conditions.flow: constant reactant flow from the burner; normal-flame total mass flow 0.6 to 12.2 mg/s and inverse-flame total mass flow 2.3 to 11.3 mg/s in the published extinction analysis

investigations.variables: Varied: reactant flow rate, fuel dilution and oxygen concentration (stoichiometric mixture fraction, adiabatic flame temperature), chamber pressure, and flow direction (normal or inverse flame). Held: ethylene with nitrogen as inert (one propane day), spherical burner. Methane, CO2 diluent and coflow flames were not tested.
measurements: broad and narrow-band flame emission (photomultiplier tubes)

findings.claim: Preliminary BRE results describe quasi-steady emulated burning corresponding to materials such as PMMA and Nylon in microgravity without air flow, with continued burning in elevated oxygen and short-time self-extinction at 21% oxygen.
findings.quote: Quasi-steady burning corresponding to various condensed-phase materials (such as PMMA and Nylon) was observed in microgravity despite the absence of air flow, where the cessation of ventilation is an established step in putting out spacecraft fires. The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time. While BRE’s results are still preliminary, they suggest that NASA may want to increase use of its alternative flammability Test 2, with the cone calorimeter, where that test can measure material properties corresponding to the microgravity flames observed with the BRE burner.

findings.claim: In BRE, low-momentum microgravity flames could burn for minutes without air flow, but self-extinguished below about 25% oxygen by volume. At elevated oxygen, larger flames generally self-extinguished within 1.5 minutes, and methane flames within a minute, while smaller or ethylene flames could burn for minutes.
findings.quote: Low-momentum microgravity flames can burn for minutes in the absence of an air flow or flame spread. While the flames can burn for minutes in elevated oxygen concentrations, like those being considered for future spacecraft, they were found to self-extinguish in concentrations below ~25% (by volume). While smaller flames can burn for minutes at elevated oxygen concentrations, larger flames were generally seen to self-extinguish within 1.5 minutes. While ethylene flames at elevated oxygen concentrations can burn for minutes, methane flames were seen to self-extinguish within a minute.
